rationale:
Revision of the candidate the Evaluator reviewed. The Evaluator found that the rationale describes outer sensors at x = ±0.040 m, but the geometry block still had ±0.032 m. I have set the geometry to match the stated intent: five sensors at x = -0.040, -0.020, 0.000, +0.020, +0.040 m, all at y = 0.07 m, with 16 mm footprints and weights [-2, -1, 0, 1, 2].

Evidence. Iteration 6 (base 0.9, kp 1.4, ki 0, kd 0.5, y 0.07, x ±0.032, last_direction) is the best raced design at 683.7. Its oval and s-bend both finished 20/20, and its slalom went off_track in all 20 runs at progress 0.392. Lead (y 0.075, iteration 8) and speed (base 0.85, iteration 7) both reduced slalom progress. Damping (kd 0.6, iteration 9) also reduced it, to 0.351. Lateral reach is the only lever not yet tested, so this revision changes only the outer span.

Change. Outer sensors widen from ±0.032 m to ±0.040 m. Everything else is held at the iteration 6 values (base_speed 0.9, kp 1.4, ki 0, kd 0.5, y 0.07, line_loss last_direction, body and wheel geometry unchanged). The off-track limit is max(0.06, 0.0125 + 0.12/4) = 0.06 m, so body width cannot help.

Expected result. Slalom progress rises above 0.40 because the outer sensors see the tape earlier on the sharp direction changes. The oval and s-bend stay at 20/20.

Decision rules for the next race. If s-bend finishes fall below 18 of 20, or s-bend steering_oscillation exceeds about 0.35, the outer sensors are seeing the tape on curves too early, so return x to ±0.032 m. If slalom progress stays near 0.39 with no change, the slalom geometry is the limit, and the final iteration should lock iteration 6 settings.

Hypotheses. (1) Wider reach raises slalom progress above 0.40 without costing s-bend finishes. (2) Wider reach adds turn gain on the s-bend, which shows up as higher oscillation there.
